text:
Nadia: Quick note from intake todaywe had a model that passed the standard microbench but blew past memory and tail latency in dedicated. Need to tighten onboarding checks.

Omar: What looked different? batch sizes, token lengths, or runtime flags?

Nadia: Two things stood out: a few long prefixes (~1k tokens) and a sudden OS OOM in the stress path when batch > 32. Bench didn't surface that because our harness caps batch at 16.

Priya: Hm. We should include a mem-stress probe that runs a worst-case concatenation of golden prompts. Even a tiny percent of intakes cause footguns if mem usage grows superlinearly.

Carlos: Agreed. Also noticed runtime kernel fallback: binary was built with fused-mha enabled but on some infra we fall back to reference kernels which allocate more temp buffers. That explains the memory swing. We need kernel_profile recorded with the intake.

Jules: Suggestion: add a "traffic-mimic" pass that runs three scenarios: short-req steady, long-prefix spikes, and high-batch stress. Each is small (5-20s) but should capture tail behaviors.

Omar: For cost reasons do quick variants first: quick-smoke (5s per scenario) and full-mimic (30s) only if quick-smoke shows delta.

Priya: Validator schema idea (compact): {"synth_p95":"95ms","mimic_p95":"180ms","mem_peak_mb":"4200","kernel_profile":"fused-mha-v2","batch_tested":"32"}. Validation: if mimic_p95/synth_p95 > 1.3 OR mem_peak_mb > mem_budget_flag -> WARN/BLOCK.

Nadia: I like mem_budget_flag. For each instance family we have budgets (A100 small mem vs 80GB, V100 etc). Validator should map instance_family -> mem_budget and compare.

Carlos: Another mismatch: bench runs with NHWC layout and prod uses NCHW for some ops, leading to slower convs for multimodal models. We should capture tensor_layout in metadata.

Jules: Also add a small "probe hammer" that intentionally creates a spill-to-disk scenario (reduce GPU cache), to see if the model gracefully degrades or OOMs. Not for every intake, but as a periodic gate.

Omar: Operational flow: 
- quick-smoke runs on PRs (ci checks)
- if quick-smoke delta > 15% or mem > 90% budget -> schedule full-mimic in dedicated infra
- if full-mimic fails -> block admission and create an ops ticket

Priya: Severity mapping: SHIELD (block), OBSERVE (do canary deploy + metrics), NOTE (store metadata). Different names than WARN/FAIL to avoid confusion with existing tooling.

ops-bot: ack. I will add label `mimic-delta` for PRs and open a canary job when severity==OBSERVE.

Nadia: UI idea: intake form should have two optional boxes: "golden sample set" (attachments) and "expected heavy prefixes" (example prompts). That speeds reviewer triage.

Carlos: Also capture `last_failed_probe` and `kernel_fallbacks` in the model record so SRE can hunt regressions automatically.

Jules: Example CLI for mimics: `./mimic_runner --binary ./builds/m.bin --scenarios short,long,stress --batch-max 64 --layout NCHW`

Priya: One more: record CPU-side stall metrics (host->gpu memcpy durations) during mimic runs. Sometimes the GPU is fine but the host queueing kills tail latency. Validator should store those numbers.

Nadia: Action items: 
- Nadia: spec mem_budget mapping + intake UI copy (due Mon 05/04).
- Omar: add quick-smoke mimic to CI + label integration (due Wed 05/06).
- Priya: validator proto + metadata fields (layout/kernel/mem_peak/host_stalls) (due Wed 05/06).
- Carlos: add kernel_profile capture to build pipeline and note common fallback reasons (due Fri 05/08).
- Jules: prototype `mimic_runner` and stress scenarios (due Fri 05/08).

Priya: I'll open the validator schema PR and link tests.

ops-bot: Reminder: canary windows will be 24h by default, configurable per team.

Nadia: Great work. Let's avoid surprises in prod; small targeted probes should catch most footguns. Ping me if blockers crop up. :rocket:
